scope: Manual close reading of crosswalk rows 111–267 (T5–T8), full transcript sources, original human coding records, and every machine claim for the same transcript. Relations judge defensible human meanings as a set. human_inference_support is separate from AI relation: unspecified rows inherit supported; an override identifies an overreach or an important qualification. machine_claim_ids are the directly relevant claims, usually the first/clearest rather than an exhaustive duplicate list. human_insight_missing means no substantively equivalent claim was found anywhere in that transcript, not merely no aligned claim.

rows.explanation: Serious illness repeatedly delayed departure; the AI directly preserves the illness and near-discharge facts (S076–77).
The human set captures both separation and the restriction on a near-military-age brother, which the AI states at S081.
The wrenching goodbye is direct evidence of separation and grief (S089).
Private passage relieved terrible conditions but consumed settlement money; the AI retains the economic sacrifice (S104).
Seasickness severe enough for ship-doctor visits is explicit in the source; no equivalent claim appears anywhere in T5’s AI inventory.

The source supports awful conditions and Friedman’s qualified recollection that a sister’s stomach was affected for life ("I think"); no T5 AI claim covers either travel harm or that lasting consequence. The qualification must remain.
Passing eye/head examinations is a direct procedural/health-check match (S129–34).
Father’s German enabled communication with examiners and was a practical arrival resource (S147).
The source joins return, parent-child separation, crying, and witnessing distress; AI retains the consequential core (S162–66).
Learning a language and escaping Jewish exclusion from higher education are named migration reasons (S211).
Unfamiliar bananas/oranges and the lunch-box episode are captured as newness at the threshold (S223–27).
Her observation that New Yorkers need not look behind them supports perceived freedom/safety (S232).
The uncle’s first meeting is explicitly a crying, kissing family reunion (S244).
Arrival at the aunt’s home provides both support and an emotional reunion (S268).
Mary Janes are a child’s concrete imagined American acquisition, not merely generic expectation (S348).
The farewell gift and sadness support leaving close people behind (S389).
Partner fraud, exhausted money, and seven-child precarity are a direct economic-hardship match (S416–23).
The lasting residue of hardship is directly retained by the AI (S441).

This passage describes a mixed neighborhood and the Jewish community’s location, but not friendship across communities. AI’s geographic claim is accurate yet does not validate C3’s friendship inference.
The established/Americanized Jewish girls’ perceived superiority is captured, including the acculturation hierarchy (S460–62).
Different values/customs and having to get used to another culture substantiate adaptation (S477–83).
Unfulfilled Mary Janes and deprivation in childhood are preserved as loss after migration (S510–11).
Perseverance and the wish that conditions had been easier for father are both retained (S535–36).
Comfort coexisted with Jewish insecurity and lack of freedom; this guards against an economic-only push account (S035–38).
Persistent insecurity despite a pleasant home is directly stated (S043).
Parental discussion makes migration an emerging aspiration; the AI preserves this cautiously (S045).
Parents’ arranging papers for other families is concrete community/migration-network support (S046).
Illness, expired passports, and repeated years of delay are all preserved (S051–54).
Father’s status protected the family from police checking (S039); this does not establish C2’s ‘wealth privilege.’ The relevant AI claim is a different, supported legal-status meaning.
Seeing Liberty prompted embracing and tears—relief/hope at arrival (S125–26).
War converted delayed separation into permanent family loss (S082–83).
The parents’ first aid to a pogrom survivor supports help to others amid danger (S060).
Maria’s icon and stand before the house is specific, unexpected protective action (S070–71).

The ornament-triggered nausea is a specific sensory form of the lasting migration hardship/emotional residue captured by AI at S441; AI is less specific but substantively covers the human impact meaning.
The direct judgment that the boat lacked basic niceties and was awful is a defensible travel-condition code with no equivalent T5 AI claim.
Holding one another and being kept together supports family solidarity during processing (S142–44).
Her cattle comparison is a direct dehumanization reading of the partitions (S167).
The doctor’s named cheer for the family after processing supports recognition of their intact passage; AI preserves that specific public acclaim.
America’s very idea made it special, supporting idealization/anticipated safety (S233).
The reciprocal waves with children are a small but grounded first social encounter with no equivalent T5 AI claim.
Renting a home, school registration, and job search are concrete early settlement/rebuilding actions with no equivalent T5 AI claim.
This is a crosswalk miss: AI claim S459 directly records close school friendships across ethnic/religious lines.
AI directly captures children feeling pre-migration tension (S291). C1’s comparative before/after formulation goes beyond this short passage, though the interview provides the broader contrast.
Fast English acquisition enabled grade skipping but left a mathematics gap; AI preserves both gain and cost (S436–37).
The artist’s unwanted commercial work is a direct livelihood compromise (S431).
Father’s illness/death left mother and daughter working, supporting both survival and gendered responsibility (S438–39).
America’s advantages are explicitly offered as the reason hardship felt worthwhile (S443).

Friedman says that after her husband’s death she felt lost, volunteered more, and that it did a great deal for her (S521–25, S551), supporting a restorative effect. AI correctly records the work; its ‘mirroring her own arrival’ causal gloss is unsupported.
Alignment misses this wording, but the AI elsewhere states that the children received what immigrants could not provide (S538); same intergenerational outcome.
A false lexical/alignment miss: the same evaluative outcome is expressed in AI’s ‘worth it’ claim at S443.
Close non-Jewish school friendships support social integration (S459).
English between children and Russian only to mother directly support language shift/loss (S494–95).
Mother learned through children and radio; family-supported language learning is directly grounded (S493–500).
Retained Russian enabled translation/outreach, a clear bilingual resource (S527–30).
Children receiving the missed opportunities supports the intergenerational-improvement code (S538).
‘No regrets’ and ‘wonderful life’ directly support a positive outcome evaluation (S541).
Father’s work-driven advance departure brings together motive, opportunity, and separation (S041ff).
Mother’s daily bread, washing, and boarding-house labor substantiate endless settlement work (S261ff).
Tears and the never-returned visit support enduring separation/loss (S049ff).
German-morning/English-afternoon school was unintelligible, directly linking language barrier and school disruption.
Old-country dress, ridicule, and not understanding the interaction directly support social exclusion (S101ff).
Reading/writing and skipped grades substantiate educational progress; C3’s difficulty label need not erase it.
Helping mother knead bread and wash directly supports child household labor.
Ten years before seeing voyage friends supports friend separation, even though C3 calls them family.
First crackers and bananas are direct sensory unfamiliarity at Ellis Island.
AI S248 records mother carrying trunk, bundle, and both children. It does not retain the human’s ‘all worldly goods’ material-precarity specificity; C3’s receiving-help label is unsupported.
‘Wash’ as the first heard/understood English word directly supports early learning.
Meeting father was explicitly joyful, confusing, and disappointing; AI preserves the reunion without flattening it.
The coal business describes sustained, physically heavy survival work.
Beds, spittoons, and four daily two-mile walks directly support child responsibility and hardship.
No interpreter and phonetic renaming are directly captured as absence of arrival help.
Two-year paternal absence, strangeness, and incomprehensible speech substantiate worry and language barrier.
Adjustment is explicitly tied to knowing enough language to understand what was happening.
Economical bread-and-beans diet supports economic hardship; C3’s discovery label is incidental.
Mother’s unpaid cooking/washing in exchange for family food is a precise household-economy account.
Changing jobs for raises and becoming a confidential secretary supports self-directed career mobility.
Mrs. Lichter’s lot-as-down-payment is unambiguous community support.
The citizenship exam demanded unusually extensive study because of her English/work history.
Punishment for Slovak in public directly supports pre-migration language suppression.
Sleeping on brick stoves for warmth is a grounded harsh-living-condition insight with no equivalent T6 AI claim.
Mother’s work at about ten, long walks, floor-sleeping and all-day labor substantiate child labor before migration.
A philanthropist’s loan financed passage; this is support from a non-kin connector.
Fetching water for unable fellow passengers directly supports mutual care on the journey; no equivalent T6 AI claim appears.
C1’s hardship/perseverance is explicit (‘hard… we survived’) but no T6 AI claim gives an equivalent survival meaning. C2’s ‘family expects too much’ is unsupported by the passage.
Mother’s shuttle between children/bundles supports a difficult, anxious journey; AI retains the maneuver.
The non-golden streets phrase directly frames expectation versus settlement reality.
Father chose Kenosha because he knew people there, a clear network resource.
Peers leaving school for maid/factory work supports early employment constrained by education.
AI S411 captures the constrained high-school route, while the human code foregrounds her desire/determination. Both are grounded but emphasize different parts of the exchange.
Mother’s infection made her daughter leave school and take over household work, supporting female survival responsibility.
Dried food lasting all the way to Kenosha supports practical journey preparation; no equivalent T6 AI claim appears.
She gives up a job for children’s presence, then takes part-time work: family over career is direct.
A friend’s migration forty years later supports an extended separation theme, with no equivalent T6 AI claim.
A false crosswalk miss: AI S171 explicitly names inability to speak English as the cause of misery on entering American school.
AI records that English/longevity shaped a demanding citizenship hearing (S494), but not the age-based need to apply independently; the accounts overlap on individual citizenship navigation.
Fewer boarders and rent from flats support gradual economic improvement.
Cleaning lamp chimneys and emptying spittoons before school is direct child household labor.
Few happy childhood memories because years were work is a valid lasting-impact insight with no equivalent T6 AI claim.
Settling where relatives/friends were known explicitly supports migrant network formation.
Hiding Michael’s boil from the doctor directly expresses fear of exclusion/deportation.
Moves between Kenosha and Racine followed available work, directly supporting employment insecurity.
Required factory work that was not easy is an explicit economic challenge with no equivalent T6 AI claim.
Serious illness could mean return and was a disaster—clear deportation fear/procedural threat.
Mitchell Motors to secretary/confidential secretary is a direct career-opportunity match.
The aunt’s daily food visits are direct family support during detention.
Batta calls the young group journey enjoyable despite its later roughness; no equivalent positive-journey claim appears in T7.
Her vivid mountain-like water and unstable boat directly substantiate harsh travel conditions; no equivalent T7 AI claim appears.
Deck waving and ‘Of course I was happy’ explicitly support arrival excitement.
A social/political chain from aunt’s contact to a presidential telegram is an unusually concrete procedural-navigation resource.

AI accurately captures friendship with Jewish people enabling access to a different kitchen (S328), which supports a narrow familiarity/resource reading. Batta is explicitly Roman Catholic, so this cannot support Jewish identity or broad cultural continuity.
Pre-existing Bohemian/German/Hungarian and English in six months support multilingual ability and rapid adaptation.
Father left at three and was not seen again until 1921: direct prolonged family separation.
Mother’s death, brother’s removal, and grandparents’ care substantiate family disruption.
War stopped letters and contact, directly supporting disrupted communication.
She says she and grandmother wanted migration, while father’s letter requests her; agency is shared rather than exclusively hers.
Attempted seizure and burning of father’s property directly support violent dispossession.
A false crosswalk miss: AI S347 identifies the thirty-two co-travellers and their practical community during detention.
The long-separated father feels strange to her; AI preserves this emotional consequence.
Domestic employment two weeks after release directly supports quick entry to work.
Hungarian strudel skill drew the household’s attention, supporting culture as occupational resource.
Fur work, skill acquisition, and 39 years in the union support an enduring career trajectory.
Grandparents’ pork store and ‘we had everything’ substantiate adequate pre-migration life.
Her aunt’s presence in New York and visit home support kin assistance in migration.
Father’s offence at the aunt and departure for Cleveland supports post-migration family tension.
Officials’ refusal to release her to her aunt supports procedural uncertainty.
Daily sending back/sending out and commotion substantiate immigration uncertainty.
The thirty-two co-travellers provided someone she could talk to, a grounded peer-support insight.
The shared gated sleeping space and girlfriend support a shared detention experience without romanticizing it.
Changing place, learning through others’ speech, and acquiring English support adaptation.
AI S454 captures the shipboard companion and her teaching him words for reunion, but not the human emphasis on daily companionship/taking him around the ship.
Filth and crawling/crackling bugs directly support poor arrival conditions.
Mother damned the voyage after Ellis Island’s filth; negative arrival evaluation/regret is direct.
Seeing skates and desiring roller shoes is a concrete unfamiliar-thing observation missed by AI.
He explicitly reports little difficulty learning English and links it to his intelligence; rapid adjustment is supported.
An Italian/Sicilian neighborhood with relations living there directly supports ethnic-community settlement; AI’s wider continuity framing should remain tied to these facts.
Neighborhood friends protected non-English speakers from boys’ harassment; community protection and language vulnerability are both direct.
Move from $14 first job to $24 Edison job supports opportunity/mobility while retaining low-wage context.
‘Free country’ is his own rationale for leaving the ship job, supporting perceived freedom and rights.
Father’s solo work migration supports both separation and economic motive.
Property, sales, rents, and uncle management substantiate pre-migration financial stability.
He explicitly becomes emotional talking about Sicily; homeland attachment is direct.
Grandfather gives houses to married boys but directs girls to husbands, a direct gendered inheritance arrangement.
Property sustained the household and paternal uncles supplied wine/support, grounding family-bond and resource readings.
Mother’s ‘man of the house’ delegation of church collection supports gendered household authority; AI adds some framing but the core is explicit.
Uncle wanted him to remain in Italian school while father insisted on migration, a direct family conflict over futures.
Remembering wool mattresses requested by father supports bringing a comfort from home; avoid treating the isolated item as broad continuity.
The illegal flask-of-wine episode is a concrete, low-level border-navigation detail omitted from alignment.
Mother expected something different—at least cleanliness—so this is a direct expectation/reality match.
Children inducing his fall and compound arm fracture supports bullying/child vulnerability but is absent from alignment.
Father’s stated pull was that girls were freer in America; AI keeps this specific motive.
Alignment misses the row but AI separately records father’s arrangements and the family’s reunification path; this is a lexical miss, not a substantive absence.
Father’s savings plus sale of crops/property proceeds directly support financial preparation.
His retained memory of mother crying for filth supports emotional arrival distress.
Three miserable rooms, hall toilet, and no running water are clear poor-housing conditions missed by alignment.
A cousin handles school-registration questions because Charles cannot, directly joining kin support and language barrier.
The school’s inability to spell Colegero and assigning Charles directly support name change/identity adaptation.
Passing Rapid Advancement and entering ninth grade directly supports educational progress.
